failures.criterion: Filter drift under the conservative rule: an unreduced command must fall wide ('it fails wide, never narrow'). A cd on the line moves the command into another module, while the fallback covers only the Run's own module
failures.evidence: An unreduced claimed line falls to the Go files of the Run's module (ci_filter_coverage.py module fallback; the working-directory comparison covers only the step's working-directory). `cd ../envoy && go test -count=1 -timeout 20m ./...` on the test job's 'Test the Go daemon' step (ci.yaml:1443, working-directory packages/daemon) still holds the pinned text, and is unreduced because it has `&`. It therefore falls to packages/daemon, which the test filter covers in full. check-ci-filters.sh exits 0 ('test: 3434 files, 0 uncovered'), though the job would test every package of packages/envoy, and round 7 counted 171 of its non-infra .go files outside the test filter. Edit reverted. Red test, commit 71dfada1 on legion/INFRA-520, in .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh: the case 'a claimed command that cds into another module of the workspace before it runs'. Its fixture binds mod and mod2 in go.work, and its filter app covers all of mod/** plus both go.mod files, so the case first passes ('passes while the command runs in its own module'). It then changes the line to `cd ../mod2 && go test ./cmd/app ./lib` and expects exit 1 and a file of mod2/ named. Command: `PATH=<python with PyYAML>:$PATH bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh` -> 'Results: 79 passed, 2 failed'. A fix with no new parsing, under the rule: an unreduced command falls to every Go file of the repository (every module, the go.work's and the nested ones like packages/envoy/infra), not to its Run's module. Then a cd, `go -C` or any other move can only widen. The cost is that every gate with an unreduced command (go_notices, envoy_smoke and any script whose line is not its text alone) needs a filter that selects any Go change in the repository.
